**Goal `performance-pass`, Stage 5 (the fixes).** Stage 4's review is whole (`docs/perf/performance-review.md`, ending in `## floor`). Old refusals have not been priced again yet.

**The regex cache answers what a fresh compile would.** In `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs`, `compiled_prepared` asks the memory ceiling for the entry's stored `search_cost` on every hit, keys on whether the compiler forced the backtracking tier, and evicts the least recently used entry one at a time (module doc § *What a compiled pattern costs*). Three unit tests cover it. The double automaton build on a miss stays, as a stated once-per-miss bound in `search_cost`'s doc. Its gap record is deleted (`docs/perf/performance-pass.md` § *What got better*).

**19 gap records owned by `performance-pass`** keep `owners --closes performance-pass` red (`bun nv owners --closes performance-pass` lists them). `bun nv scaling --check` passes, with `numbers/bigint-mul` unclear. *Decisions for you* in `docs/perf/performance-pass.md` has two entries: a total deadline for the request head, and `Markup` concatenation in place.

next.title: the fixes, the cache tier's order queue

items.text: **A forgotten cache key takes its eviction slot with it** (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/cache.rs:976`), per `data/gaps/nvs-stdlib/a-forgotten-cache-key-leaves-its-order-slot.json`. `Entries::forget` leaves its slot in `order`, and a later `put` of the same key pushes a second one (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/cache.rs:953`), so put, forget and put grows `order` with traffic when `max_size` is off. A put with an elapsed lifetime (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/cache.rs:935`) takes the same path. Rule: AGENTS.md priority ordering (O(in-flight), not O(requests served)).

**An expired entry is removed on `get`** (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/cache.rs:985`), per the same gap record, so keys written once with a lifetime do not stay forever with the cap off. Ladder `benches/scaling/cache/forget.nvs` under `serve` if the counts can see it.
